A.explanation: Too small by a factor of 10, likely from a mm to m conversion error for the $210 \text{ mm}$ by $300 \text{ mm}$ area or the $0.1 \text{ mm}$ thickness.

B.explanation: Volume of one sheet is about $6.3 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}^3$ and $m = \rho V$ gives about $5.0 \times 10^{-3} \text{ kg} = 5 \text{ g}$.

C.explanation: Too large by a factor of 10, likely from using the $50 \text{ mm}$ pack thickness as the thickness of one sheet divided incorrectly.

D.explanation: Far too large, likely from forgetting to divide the $50 \text{ mm}$ pack thickness by 500 and from mm to m errors.

hints: First find the thickness of one sheet from the $50 \text{ mm}$ thickness of 500 sheets.
Recall density links mass and volume as $\rho = m/V$, so you need the volume $V = \text{length} \times \text{width} \times \text{thickness}$ for one sheet.
Convert all $\text{mm}$ lengths to $\text{m}$ before multiplying, then convert the mass in $\text{kg}$ to $\text{g}$ to compare with the options.
walkthrough: Thickness of one sheet is $t = 50 \text{ mm} / 500 = 0.1 \text{ mm} = 1.0 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}$.
Convert the sheet area to metres: width $= 210 \text{ mm} = 0.21 \text{ m}$ and length $= 300 \text{ mm} = 0.30 \text{ m}$.
Volume of one sheet is $V = 0.21 \times 0.30 \times 1.0 \times 10^{-4} = 6.3 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}^3$.
Use $m = \rho V$ with $\rho = 800 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$: $m = 800 \times 6.3 \times 10^{-6} = 5.04 \times 10^{-3} \text{ kg}$.
Convert to grams: $5.04 \times 10^{-3} \text{ kg} \times 1000 = 5.04 \text{ g}$, about $5 \text{ g}$. This is option B.
